data.title: Sky Sets Debt Ceilings to Zero for Five Maker Vault Types, Halting New DAI Borrowing
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing The Defiant, decentralized stablecoin protocol Sky, formerly MakerDAO, has paused new DAI borrowing across five Maker vault types backed by ETH and wstETH by setting their debt ceilings to zero.

Users can no longer mint new DAI through these vaults. Existing borrowers can still repay debt and manage collateral, but their positions remain exposed to liquidation risk.

data.title: ASIA MARKET OPEN | Asian Stocks Open Higher After Jensen Huang Returns to Nvidia; TAIEX Jumps 2,337 Points, KOSPI up 3.64%
data.description:
According to Kabutan, Yonhap and HKET, Asian stocks opened higher on Tuesday after Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. Tokyo's Nikkei 225 opened at 57,009.99, up 573.34 points, while the TOPIX opened at 3,701.61, up 27.39 points. Gains widened after the open, with the Nikkei at 58,951 as of 01:00 UTC, up 2,515 points, with Advantest contributing about 781 points. Nonferrous metals, banks and electrical machinery led sector gains, with KOKUSAI, Murata Manufacturing and Tokyo Electron among the risers.

Seoul's KOSPI opened 3.64% higher at 4,880.16, up 171.62 points, while the KOSDAQ opened at 654.31, up 18.86 points. The Korea Exchange activated a buy-side sidecar on the KOSPI at 00:06 UTC, suspending program trading for five minutes. As of 00:15 UTC, the KOSPI was up 267.61 points, or 5.68%, at 4,976.15. Samsung Electronics rose 7.35% and SK hynix gained 8.48%. The won was quoted at 1,340.8 per dollar.

Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index opened 243 points higher at 22,627, with turnover of HK$8.15 billion, while the Hang Seng Tech Index rose 2% to 3,579. Alibaba gained more than 4% and SMIC rose more than 3%, while Lenovo opened 10% higher and NetEase fell 0.9%.

Taiwan's TAIEX opened at 39,148.91, up 2,337.02 points, and extended gains to 39,621.92 as of 01:00 UTC, up 2,810.03 points, or about 7.63%. TSMC opened at its daily limit-up price of NT$2,230, up NT$200, or 9.85%.

In mainland China, all four major indexes opened higher, with the Shanghai Composite up 0.82%, the Shenzhen Component up 2.43%, the ChiNext Index up 3.88% and the STAR Composite Index up 3.94%.

data.title: U.S. Government Divisions Over Nvidia Become Public, Sources Say
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, a person familiar with the White House said divisions within the U.S. government over Nvidia had become public, partly after Chief of Staff Susie Wiles resigned on November 5, several days after Republicans suffered a major midterm election defeat. Wiles had tightly controlled officials’ public messaging. U.S. President Donald Trump appointed adviser Stephen Miller to succeed her, and Miller reportedly gave Cabinet members greater autonomy. Sources said officials were now able to speak out ahead of the administration and sometimes publicly take positions at odds with the president.

By last weekend, some White House officials who had been skeptical of Jensen Huang had softened their stance. On Sunday, Bessent’s remarks appeared to suggest that the U.S. government did not necessarily consider Huang personally responsible for issues involving compliance with rules for Nvidia chips.

data.title: Ethereum Co-Founder Joseph Lubin Promotes Synchronous Composability Technology
data.description: Ethereum co-founder Joseph Lubin promoted synchronous composability technology in a post. According to Foresight News, Lubin said the technology could let financial institutions and market infrastructure use both private and public networks, operating private Besu networks while transacting with other private EVM networks, Layer 2 networks, and Ethereum Layer 1 without cross-chain bridges. He said this could unify fragmented execution environments and liquidity pools.

data.title: predict.fun Puts 76ers’ Win Probability at 51% as They Tie Trail Blazers 69-69 at Halftime
data.description:
The Philadelphia 76ers and Portland Trail Blazers were tied 69-69 at halftime in their NBA regular-season game. According to Odaily, predict.fun listed the probability of a 76ers win at 51% during the break.

The game began at 8 a.m. today, with Philadelphia hosting Portland in the 2026-2027 season. Before the game, the 76ers were 14-3, tied with the Lakers for the league’s best record, and had won five straight. They beat the Milwaukee Bucks 132-129 in their previous game. Portland opened the season 10-6 and had lost three of its previous four games, including a 97-96 loss to the New York Knicks after a Bridges three-pointer at the buzzer.

Joel Embiid was out sick. Philadelphia’s starters were Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown, James and Jabari Walker. Brown returned but was under a minutes restriction; Adem Bona also returned after missing eight consecutive games. Ja Morant, Shaedon Sharpe, Vit Krejci and Yang Bulade were out injured for Portland. Maxey was averaging 25.9 points per game this season, while Deni Avdija was averaging 23.9 points and six assists.

data.title: Jonathan Turley: Four Claims in Trump's $15B New York Times Suit Advance
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing The Hill, George Washington University law professor Jonathan Turley wrote that U.S. President Donald Trump secured procedural advances in two defamation lawsuits last week. Florida federal district judge Steven D. Merryday allowed four of the seven original claims in Trump’s $15 billion suit against The New York Times to proceed. The case concerns a story by Susanne Craig and Russ Buettner titled “Lucky Loser.” Merryday said the article raised the possibility of complex tax fraud and money laundering without formal legal opinions or forensic audits, and that the experts cited lacked a solid factual basis.

In a separate case, Florida judge Jeffrey Kuntz allowed Trump’s lawsuit against the BBC to proceed. The BBC documentary “Trump: A Second Chance,” aired the week before the 2024 U.S. election, spliced together two remarks from Trump’s January 6, 2021, speech that were 55 minutes apart. Kuntz wrote that the edit could support an initial inference of “actual malice,” noting the BBC had possessed the full speech for nearly three years.

Turley also said Trump lost cases against The Wall Street Journal and CNN, and appealed to the U.S. Supreme Court for a second time over the $83.3 million Carroll verdict.

data.title: Sentora Supplies 99.99% of RLUSD in Morpho XRP-Collateral Lending Market
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing CryptoSlate, Sentora’s vault supplied about 8.15 million RLUSD, or 99.99% of the market’s supply, in Morpho’s Ethereum FXRP/RLUSD lending market on November 23. The market had about 7.12 million RLUSD in outstanding loans and 1.02 million RLUSD in available liquidity, with 87.45% utilization and a 4.99% floating borrow rate. Morpho’s liquidity API showed that, with supply unchanged, borrowing an additional approximately 207,500 RLUSD would raise utilization to 90%; no additional RLUSD could be routed into the market through Public Allocator. Morpho’s rate model uses 90% as a reference point, after which the interest-rate curve steepens, though borrowing can continue while funds remain available. In a separate on-chain transaction, a wallet borrowed 1,500 RLUSD against 3,000 FXRP.

data.title: LayerZero Opens ZRO Staking; Foundation Plans to Stake 100 Million Tokens
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, LayerZero said ZRO staking is now open, and its foundation plans to stake 100 million ZRO under the same terms as other participants. data.title: Robinhood Chain Pays 70% More Than Base for Ethereum Settlement, Collects 64% Less in Fees
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing CryptoSlate, which compiled growthepie data, Robinhood Chain paid about $25,700 in Ethereum settlement fees from October 23 to November 21, 2026, around 70% more than Base’s $15,100. Over the same period, Robinhood Chain collected about $1.07 million in transaction fees, compared with Base’s $2.97 million. For every $100 in user fees collected, Robinhood Chain spent about $2.41 on Ethereum settlement, while Base spent about $0.51.

Base published about 350,000 blobs during the period, nearly twice Robinhood Chain’s 182,000. Blob fees were about $4,478 for Base and $2,315 for Robinhood Chain. Excluding blob fees, Robinhood Chain’s other settlement expenses were about $23,400, compared with Base’s $10,600. Robinhood Chain’s settlement expenses exceeded Base’s in each of the four full weeks through November 21.

data.title: Chainflip Reports About $12.6 Million in Treasury Assets Transferred, Cites Possible Network Library Vulnerability
data.description:
Chainflip said attackers transferred nearly all funds from its Bitcoin and Ethereum vaults on November 21, with preliminary findings pointing to a vulnerability in a third-party networking library. According to Odaily, the incident report said the attackers moved about 133.34 BTC, 520.22 ETH, 3,249,600 USDC and 758,100 USDT, worth about $12.6 million at prices that morning. The transactions had valid vault signatures but were generated by an attacker outside the network and were not initiated by the Chainflip protocol.

Initial findings suggest the attacker registered a validator account with the minimum stake. Although the account was not part of the active validator set, its registration allowed other validators to accept its peer-to-peer connection. The attacker then exploited a memory-safety vulnerability in a third-party networking library used by validator software, ran code on validator machines and extracted key shares to sign vault transactions without participation from the network. Chainflip said some details remain unconfirmed and the investigation is ongoing.

Swaps, deposits and withdrawals remain paused. The stolen Bitcoin has not been moved, while assets on the Ethereum side were converted to ETH and transferred to Tornado Cash. Chainflip said it has contacted law enforcement, enlisted ZeroShadow to help trace and recover the funds, and offered the attacker a bounty for returning the assets.

data.title: Opus 5.5 Rates GPT-6 Astra-Designed Tests 0.2 Points Above Human Scores
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing METR, Opus 5.5 was the AI judge whose assessments most closely matched human graders in a task evaluating AI-designed tests. However, it rated tests proposed by GPT-6 Astra about 0.2 points higher than human graders on a scale of 0 to 1.

METR said the gap could affect whether its evaluation rules recommend spending more time developing the tests. None of the tasks designed by the models in the evaluation met the practical standard for inclusion in METR’s report.

In backtests of 15 historical programming contests, Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra had median results in the 96th to 98th percentile among human participants. In the median contest, about four human contestants outperformed the strongest model.

data.title: Inkling 2 Mini Gets 36 of 43 Right on Plotly Test, Including 1 of 5 Hidden-Mode Questions
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Plotly, Thinking Machines Lab’s open-weight model Inkling 2 Mini answered 36 of 43 data analysis questions correctly, an 84% score. The model, released on November 20, got all 20 standard analysis questions right but answered only one of five hidden-mode questions correctly.

Plotly said the model made 585 queries on one hidden-mode question over about 48 minutes without finding the answer. It also correctly answered five ambiguous questions and five unfulfillable requests, along with two data quality questions and three statistical trap questions. Plotly noted that the score was based on a single sample.

data.title: 1.557 Million SOL Worth $112.5 Million Transferred to FalconX After Staking Exit
data.description: An address transferred 1.557 million SOL, valued at $112.5 million, to institutional trading platform FalconX after withdrawing the tokens from staking. According to Odaily, on-chain analyst Ember tracked the transfer, which followed a rebound sparked by Lao Huang’s return.
